newsitem.title: GERMANY: TNT takes Deutche post to court over parcels contract.
newsitem.headline: TNT takes Deutche post to court over parcels contract.

text.p: TNT Logistik said it has applied for a court injunction to stop Deutsche Post AG from terminating a parcels contract worth several hundred million marks.
The contract annulment threatened more than a thousand jobs in Germany, TNT Logistik, a division of global express company TNT, claimed in a statement.

Deutsche Post cancelled the five-year agreement, due to end on March 31, 2000, with effect from June 30, 1997, on the grounds that TNT was now owned by its competitor, the Dutch post office (Koninklijke PTT Nederland N.V), TNT said.
But the recent takeover by KPN had no impact on TNT's business relationship with Deutsche Post, it added.

TNT said that under the contract, which started in 1995, it had set up a subsidiary, TNT NetLog, with 105 own staff, 35 partner firms and some 1,000 vehicles, to transport parcels in containers between 33 Deutsche Post freight centres.
TNT chairman Germany, Vinzenz Wagner, said: "The premature termination of the contract is completely inexplicable for us."
Deutsche Post had been fully satisfied with the quality of the TNT parcels service to date, he added.
The jobs of more than 1,100 TNT NetLog staff and employees of partner companies had been put at risk by the cancellation, Wagner said.
TNT spokesman Markus Wohler added that the contract was worth "several hundred million marks a year".
Deutsche Post spokesman Martin Dopychai said the KPN takeover of TNT had a major impact on the contract and thus justified the termination.
"The Dutch post office is a very aggressive competitor and through TNT they could gain internal Deutsche Post information. Therefore we had to cancel the contact," he said.
Deutsche Post rejected the claim that jobs were at risk since it wanted to continue using the sub-contractors who currently drove for TNT, Dopychai said.
It had also offered to buy out TNT NetLog but this had been rejected by KPN, he added.

Should the court decision on March 13 go in favour of Deutsche Post, then the post office would run the network itself, otherwise it would consider its legal position. - Reuters ir Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
